learning_outcomes.text: Understanding and mastery of the basic concepts of the general laws of mechanics, thermodynamics, fields and waves, and electromagnetism, and their application to solve problems typical of engineering.
Apply the acquired knowledge to identify, formulate, and solve problems in broad contexts, being able to integrate them by working in multidisciplinary teams.
Possess the learning skills that allow continuous study throughout life for adequate professional development.
Know and apply knowledge of basic sciences and technologies to the practice of Industrial Engineering.
Be able to collect, process, critically analyze, and interpret experimental data. Attitudes of critical reasoning and creative actions to approach and solve problems.
Acquire the necessary skills to apply physical knowledge to research, development, and innovation in Engineering.
Knowledge and thinking and reasoning capacities necessary for the analysis, approach, and resolution of specific problems.
Know how to apply the scientific method and scientific-technological language to solve specific engineering problems.
Acquire the necessary skills for the handling and utilization of measurement equipment, devices, and systems.

syllabus_topics: Kinematics and dynamics of the particle
Dynamics of systems and rigid bodies
assessment_rules: The final grade (NF) in the ordinary call will be the highest obtained between the progressive evaluation and the global test. To pass, a minimum grade in each part is required, and the final grade must be 5.0 out of 10 or higher. If the minimum grade in any part is not reached, the final grade cannot exceed 4.5. Grades of 5.0 or higher in theory or laboratory exams obtained in the ordinary call will be maintained for the extraordinary call, with the highest qualification between calls being considered. The progressive evaluation uses the formula NF = 24%EP + 56%EPT + 20%EL (minimums: EP >= 4/10, EPT >= 4/10, EL >= 5/10). The global test and extraordinary call use the formula NF = 80%ET + 20%EL (minimums: ET >= 4/10, EL >= 5/10).
